Each dot is one member serving on Nov. 26, 2026.

A tie is a public record. It can include the member’s criticism or outside spending against the member.

Start with the company: its employees’ own gifts, and its PAC’s.

What counts as a tie: the eleven kinds of record

The network includes Anthropic, the funders behind it, the groups they fund, and their PACs and lobbyists. Coefficient Giving, then called Open Philanthropy, named Dustin Moskovitz and Cari Tuna as its main funders. It awarded Georgetown’s CSET $55.0M in 2019. The record includes 19 committee appearances by CSET witnesses.

Each bar counts all serving members with that kind of record. 119 of the 452 members with a tie have only records of what third parties did. For those members, every kind on file comes from the second group.

I · The arrival

At the end of 2024, 10 members now serving had received money from Anthropic’s employees or its PAC. By Sept. 30, 2026: 197.

The employees gave their own money: $5.9M, 92% of it dated 2026. The company’s PAC made its first gift on record to a member now serving on June 29, 2026; by Sept. 30 it had given $200K to 81 members, 17 of whom had no gift from an employee.

Source: FEC contribution records in this project’s tables: contributions to the campaign, leadership PAC or single-member joint fundraising committee of a serving member, through Sept. 30, 2026; ANTHROPAC is Anthropic PBC’s political action committee.

A person’s contribution is their own money, not their employer’s. Employer is as the giver reported it to the FEC. Both counts are of the members serving on Nov. 26, 2026; the record stops at Sept. 30, 2026.

$6.1M in all. The large money moved another way.

Every gift on record to a member now serving (1,065 from Anthropic’s employees, 87 from its PAC), who gave, and where it landed

Through Sept. 30, 2026. The first chart’s scale is logarithmic: each line is ten times the one below; dots are translucent, so a bright patch is many gifts of one size on nearby dates. Givers are not named here; two people who share a first name and a surname count as one. A total is what the committees received, not what a member asked for. Among the largest recipients, Republicans are more than half of the five largest and of every longer list up to fourteen.

II · The bigger money

Anthropic announced $40.0M for Public First Action. There the trail stops: no filing in this record lists the group’s donors.

Separate FEC filings show receipts from Public First Action at 6 committees. The largest spending total for one candidate was $15.0M for Alexander Bores, outside Congress.

Sources include Anthropic’s announcements and FEC receipt and outside-spending filings.

In the 2020, 2022 and 2024 election cycles, Dustin Moskovitz gave $100M to Future Forward (FF PAC).

Another kind of giving reaches more members: lobbyists’ own gifts.

III · The lobbying

Lobbyists’ own gifts reach the most members: $1.8M went to campaigns or committees linked to 356 serving members.

Counted: a gift whose giver was a registered lobbyist at a firm that had a network client in that period. Each lit seat has a campaign or committee linked to a gift.

Lobbyists’ semi-annual contribution reports to Congress. Gifts dated Feb. 19, 2021 to June 30, 2026. Filed recipient names, and committee records where the filing gives them, identify the member for each counted gift.

The gift is the lobbyist’s own money. The record does not say why it was made. Named lobbyists only: $1.3M in 1,022 gifts.

Anthropic’s own lobbying is on a different record. What did the company report?

Lobbyists’ personal gifts by election cycle

118 lobbyists at 23 firms made 1,492 gifts linked to 164 Democrats, 191 Republicans and 1 independent. The total has grown in each cycle. Lobbyists’ gifts reached 356 members from Feb. 2021 to June 2026. Gifts from Anthropic employees or its PAC reached 197 from Oct. 2022 to Sept. 2026.

III · The lobbying

In the first nine months of 2026, Anthropic reported $5.6M in lobbying expenses, more than $3.1M in all of 2025.

A record of ties, not a record of influence.
